items.title: Dave Bennett interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 16, 2025
items.q: I had a friend of mine that played piano for me, Tad Weed, who was an amazing jazz teacher too.

ctx.x: That’s saying a lot. Was there a point where you started to realize, you know you’re learning these improvisations by ear? When did you connect to keys and form and relate what he was playing to chords?

Chords came much later. But as far as knowing keys and form when I was 13 my dad saw an ad in the local paper and it said the Clarkston — Clarkston is a town right near where I live here. I live in Waterford, Michigan. And it said that the Clarkston Senior Center, they were having, every Tuesday, a jam session for anybody that wanted to come to play, one until four. So he took me over there and there was a group of old timers that would get together and jam every Tuesday. And I joined them every week. So when…
I know what you mean. It’s surprising after like oh my God it’s been like twelve months since I actually sat in an ensemble and read a chart.
